source.title: Improving Weak-to-Strong Generalization with Reliability-Aware Alignment

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Runs weak-to-strong fine-tuning and reports PGR, following the Burns et al. measure, on new model pairings and datasets; it also tests reliability-aware changes to the training recipe.
record.gate_note: The study reports PGR and accuracy for naive, sampled-data, and full-data versions of two reliability-aware methods. Rows below capture PGR for the naive baseline and full-data methods. Reliability-score versus label-correctness plots and entropy-group accuracy plots are discussed but not entered as rows because they do not measure the strong student's weak-to-strong performance. Sampled-data PGR results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes strong LLMs on weak-model labels and reports PGR as Burns et al. define it, across four model pairings and four datasets. It compares naive fine-tuning with two training changes, uncertainty filtering and reliability re-weighting, so its own results bear on V1, V2 and V3.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say prompt-variation reliability scores identify correct weak labels, and that filtering and re-weighting improve weak-to-strong generalization over naive alignment. Their text says filtering 'consistently outperforms' naive, but Table 1 shows exceptions (MMLU Mistral-7B, GSM8K Llama2-13B). For re-weighting they name only GSM8K Llama2-13B as an exception.
record.recipe_differences: Retains the weak-supervisor labeling, strong-model SFT, and PGR evaluation framework, while adding prompt variation and reliability-based filtering or loss re-weighting; uses different datasets and model pairings.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by dataset, supervisor/student pairing, and whether uncertainty filtering or reliability re-weighting is used. The paper also reports sampled-data variants, but those PGR values are not extracted here.

fits_no_version.finding: Agreement across reordered or paraphrased prompts (entropy, empirical probability) tracks the weak supervisor's label correctness: accuracy falls monotonically as entropy rises (Figs 3–6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A weak supervisor's self-consistency under prompt variation predicts which of its labels are correct.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or error bars are reported for the table results. PGR is invalid in settings where the weak model performs better than the strong ceiling. The paper notes computational overhead from repeated querying and that effectiveness depends on weak-supervisor quality.
record.rows_left_out: Sampled-data PGR rows (w2s+filter.(s.) and w2s+rew.(s.)) from Tables 1 and 2 are omitted; they are additional method/data-size conditions. Accuracy values are omitted in favor of the directly relevant PGR measure. Reliability-quality plots in Figures 3–6 and Appendix D are summarized in gate_note, not extracted as student-performance rows.

untested.parts: Auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling of weak supervisors, and other loss variants from the original.
Chess and reward modelling; representations as predictors of PGR; no systematic sweep of supervisor or student size (only four fixed pairings).
Not tested: exploitation of supervisor blind spots, distribution shift, error similarity.

missing.what: Sampled-data (size-matched) PGR for filtering and re-weighting. These are the controlled comparison for V2, because full-data methods use the augmented dataset.
missing.locator: Tables 1 and 2, rows w2s+filter.(s.) and w2s+rew.(s.)

missing.what: Accuracy for pairings where PGR is invalid (Mistral-7B to Llama3-8B on Hellaswag and ETHICS). It shows naive students below the weak model and the methods recovering.

record.verdict_notes: All values were checked against Tables 1 and 2 and recomputed from accuracy. Naive weak-to-strong often fails here: on ETHICS every student scores below its supervisor. Full-data method gains are partly confounded with extra training data from prompt augmentation. No error bars are reported, and GSM8K accuracies are very low (around 0.06–0.13), so PGR there is noisy.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test all settings in the original work; tests the stated LLM pairings and four datasets.
Tests uncertainty filtering and reliability re-weighting; does not test auxiliary confidence loss, weak-supervisor ensembling, or other loss variants.
Varies student/supervisor model pairing and task across four datasets. Does not test chess, reward modelling, or representations as predictors of PGR.
No tests of exploitable supervisor blind spots, distribution shift, or shared error patterns.
No theory establishing conditions under which students must beat supervisors.
Language benchmarks only; no vision experiments.
